newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suez/Lyonnaise eyes growth in telecom sector.
newsitem.headline: Suez/Lyonnaise eyes growth in telecom sector.

text.p: Suez/Lyonnaise, the new company formed by the merger of Suez and Lyonnaise des Eaux SA, will decide in autumn whether to invest in the telecommunications sector, company officials said on Saturday.
In an interview with Radio Classique, the group's top managers also ruled out limiting future alliances in the sector to French partners.
"Suez-Lyonnaise is in a position to chose its partners. All options are open ... Decisions will be taken probably in autumn ...," said Suez chairman Gerard Mestrallet.
He said Lyonnaise's cable television network offered a good basis to get into the telecom sector.

"There can only be international consortiums and therefore we are at the moment considering and studying opportunities of (setting up) consortiums with foreign compagnies," Lyonnaise chairman Jerome Monod said, adding these partners could be European or American.
Monod repeated that the group would earn at least 3.5 billion francs in net profit in 1997 and hoped to double that in five years.
Revenue generated by the four core sectors -- water, energy, waste treatment and communications -- was expected to jump to 180 billion francs in five years from a current 100 billion, he said.
